Question: What is the purpose of issuing grades in middle school? This is a serious question and I would love some input from educators. I am a student, it stems from a conversation, and I am trying to gain perspective.
Answer: Huh? For the USA: One needs a measure of where the student “stands” relative to the expected learning for each course/subject in every year of school. Middle school is the transition from elementary school where the grades may be: Exceptional, Satisfactory, Needs more work, Failing; to high school where the grades may be A, B, C, D, F and some with “pluses or minuses”. In my high school our grades were numerical, 75 was failing and the grades went up to 100. The assumption being, if you didn’t absorb and understand at least 75% of the material that you were expected to cover in that subject during that term or year, then you will be lost as you try to advance in the subject’s material in the subsequent years. Simple and logical. How else would the student know if they are truly understanding the required material, if they do not get a Grade from the teachers? By getting a grade in middle school, you are preparing yourself for high school where your GPA may determine your ability to apply to colleges, the US military and/or various jobs. Good luck.

Question: Are there any non-black or non-grey stealth aircraft used by the US military, such as fighter jets?

The current F-22, F-35 and the B-2A all operate in tactics and methodologies to keep a great distance between themselves and the enemy so that they are mere pixels at a great distance. If they are flying very high, the background of deep space is Black, and the blue-gray that is used top and bottom allows those aircraft, as “pixels” to be generally unseen. Indeed the B-2A goes to Great length to prevent a contrail from forming as most high flying aircraft are “visible” because of their contrails. Note that “blue-gray” coloration also works well if the aircraft is flying very low and enemy satellites or high flying aircraft are trying to locate them….. Mere pixels in the enemy’s view. Simple and logical.
